parameters.content:
## 03 - Reply Handler C2
Receives customer replies forwarded by `03r - Inbound Router` (Twilio's sandbox allows one inbound
URL for both case studies). Reachable on its own path, so it can be tested without the router.

Order: match cart by phone (30 days) -> record the inbound -> opt-out -> classify -> route.
An unmatched phone exits silently with a log row: replying "who are you?" to a stranger is worse
than saying nothing.

The touch schedule is NEVER modified here except by an opt-out. A customer asking about delivery
has not withdrawn consent, and touch 2 still has a job to do.

nodes.name: Note - Opt-out is a compliance control, not a classification

parameters.content:
## Opt-out is a compliance control, not a classification
The keyword check runs BEFORE the model and short-circuits straight to suppression. We tell the
customer "reply STOP" / "للإيقاف أرسل: توقف", so a customer who does exactly that must be honoured
with certainty rather than with high probability - the same rule that keeps the recovery link and
the opt-out line out of the model's hands.

The model still has an `opt_out` class for the phrasings a keyword list cannot catch ("please
don't message me again", "لا أريد رسائل"), and is told to lean toward suppression when unsure.

Suppression is permanent and per cart: `opted_out = true`, `next_touch_at = null`, status
`opted_out`. The PATCH filters on `opted_out=eq.false`, so a second STOP updates 0 rows and cannot
send a second confirmation. `Fetch Due Carts` in workflow 02 already excludes opted-out carts, so
touches 2 and 3 stop by construction.

nodes.notes:
Writes the inbound reply to cart_messages AND acts as the idempotency lock (M5.2b).

Twilio retries an inbound webhook it does not get a timely 200 for. `uniq_cart_messages_inbound_sid` (partial unique index on twilio_message_id where direction='inbound') turns that retry into a 409 here, which `Is Duplicate Inbound` routes to a log-and-exit - so the customer never gets a second holding reply for one message they sent once.

Insert-as-lock, not SELECT-then-INSERT: two concurrent retries can both pass a read check, but only one can win the unique index. fullResponse is what makes the 409 visible; neverError keeps it out of the error path since a duplicate is a normal event, not a failure.

nodes.name: Suppress Cart

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ opted_out: true, next_touch_at: null, status: 'opted_out' }) }}

nodes.notes:
Suppresses EVERY open cart for this phone, not one cart id.

Until 2026-09-02 this filtered id=eq.<the one cart pickCart chose>, so a customer holding two live carts who sent توقف had ONE suppressed and kept receiving touches from the other.

The status filter is the guard that matters: it restricts the write to OPEN carts, so a cart already closed as recovered / converted_before_first_touch is never overwritten and the converted_after_opt_out distinction survives. opted_out=eq.false keeps the write idempotent on a repeat STOP.

rows_updated can now legitimately be 2+; Log Opt-Out Run treats >= 1 as success.

nodes.name: Is Duplicate Inbound
nodes.notes: 409 = the unique index rejected this MessageSid, i.e. Twilio is retrying a webhook we already handled. TRUE stops here. Any other status (201 on a fresh insert, or a Supabase error) continues: a logging failure must never swallow a real customer reply.

nodes.name: Log Duplicate Inbound

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify((function(){ var c = $('Resolve Reply Context').first().json; return { workflow_name: '03 - Reply Handler C2', execution_id: $execution.id, cart_id: c.cart_id, status: 'success', step_name: 'duplicate_inbound', metadata: { checkout_token: c.checkout_token, twilio_sid: c.inbound_sid, phone: c.phone, route_it_would_have_taken: c.route, action: 'dropped_no_reply_sent' } }; })()) }}

nodes.notes: A dropped duplicate MUST leave a row. 'Nothing happened' is indistinguishable from a webhook that never arrived - the exact silent-loss shape that hid the dead tunnel and the workflow-04 Switch defect in M4. status=success because dropping a retry is correct behaviour, not a failure.

nodes.name: Record Phone Suppression

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify((function(){ var c = $('Resolve Reply Context').first().json; var src = c.keyword_hit ? 'keyword' : 'model_intent'; return { phone: c.phone, source: src, cart_id: c.cart_id, keyword_hit: c.keyword_hit || null, note: 'opt-out via workflow 03, execution ' + $execution.id }; })()) }}

nodes.notes:
THE COMPLIANCE BOUNDARY. Written BEFORE the cart PATCH on purpose: if the row write failed after the carts were already suppressed, future carts from this phone would be unprotected - the failure that actually matters. This way the worst case is a suppressed phone whose old carts were not patched, and the sweep's case2_due_carts anti-join already excludes those.

phone is the PRIMARY KEY, so a repeat STOP is a no-op: Prefer resolution=ignore-duplicates turns the 409 into a 200.

nodes.name: Stamp Last Inbound
nodes.notes:
Opens the 24-hour WhatsApp service window on this cart (2026-09-03). Workflow 02 reads it to record whether the next touch would be a free-form session message or a paid Meta template.

WHY IT SITS HERE. Downstream of Is Duplicate Inbound on purpose: a Twilio webhook retry hits the 409 idempotency lock in Log Inbound Message and exits before this node, so a redelivery cannot restamp a window the customer did not reopen. Upstream of Route Reply Path, so every inbound stamps it - including one that turns out to be an opt-out, because the customer did reply either way.

WHY ONLY id=eq. AND NO STATUS GUARD. Every other cart writer in this build filters on status and opted_out, because they move status, next_touch_at or touches_sent and a stale writer can resurrect a closed cart. This one writes a single timestamp and moves none of those, so it cannot resurrect anything, and stamping a cart that closed mid-flight is simply true. Do not 'fix' this by adding the guards - it would silently stop recording replies on exhausted carts, which are exactly the ones a customer answers late.

A failed stamp degrades safely: the column stays null, workflow 02 classifies the next touch as 'template', and the only cost is an over-estimate of template spend.
